Project Structure

Discover & Define: We conducted a user research study to gain deeper insights into the pain points and challenges users face. Through in-depth interviews with 10 participants, we explored their experiences, frustrations, and needs, which helped us uncover critical patterns and areas for improvement.

Ideate & Wireframe: We brainstormed various solutions based on user insights, focusing on functionality, usability, and user experience. We refined the best concepts and moved forward with designs that prioritize user needs while ensuring a seamless and intuitive interaction.

User Test: Based on the lo-fi prototypes, we generated high-fidelity prototypes that we eventually tested with our participants.

Problem Space

Riders of traditional motorcycle dashboards face significant issues with visibility under varying lighting conditions and an overload of information that complicates quick data retrieval.

Riders expressed frustration with cluttered displays, limited customization, and the lack of real-time information on existing dashboards.

How-Might-We's

I spoke with 10 riders to understand their pain points and preferences and I also studied existing motorcycle dashboards and smart devices. To better understand and empathize the users, I observed riders using their dashboards in various conditions.

User Stories

"Sometimes I feel overwhelmed by all the data on the dashboard. I want the most important information to be highlighted, so I can quickly glance at my speed and battery level without distraction"

"When I'm riding in bright sunlight, I often struggle to see the dashboard clearly. I wish there were options to adjust the brightness or switch to a mode that makes the information easier to read"

"It would be amazing if the dashboard could integrate with my phone, so I can see navigation prompts, notifications, and riding stats directly on the screen"

"I would prefer seeing my riding stats and history like average speed and distance traveled on the dashboard itself."

Through these conversations and observations, it became clear that riders desired a dashboard that was not only easy to navigate but also enhanced their overall riding experience.
After the research it was clear on what we needed to focus. Follwong are the things we needed to prioritise and work on.

Ideation

During the ideation phase, I employed the Double Diamond method to explore and refine solutions for the bike dashboard. After identifying key user pain points, such as lack of information clarity and non-interactive screens, I facilitated brainstorming sessions and gathered insights from riders to better understand their needs.

Using this feedback, I developed multiple sketches and wireframes, focusing on intuitive design and seamless integration with the bike app. After this, I moved on to hi-fi design for concept.


Image: Hi-Fi Designs concept

Development

I collaborated closely with the embedded engineering team to bring the dashboard design to life. This collaboration was instrumental in bridging the gap between design and technology, enabling me to approach future projects with a more holistic perspective.

Key Features - Hi-Fi Designs

Ride Modes


There are three ride modes available: Suste, Babaal, and Thikka. Users can switch between these modes using a button located on the handlebar. To enhance the user experience, we implemented a stacked layout with smooth scroll animations, allowing riders to effortlessly navigate and switch between the modes. The scroll feature provides a seamless transition, making it easy for users to select their preferred riding experience.

KPI Metrics


At the top of the dashboard, the user's name appears on the left, adding a personal touch and sense of ownership. On the right, essential indicators such as battery level, network, Bluetooth, and GPS icons are displayed. This layout ensures users can quickly check their vehicle's status while maintaining a personalized and user-friendly experience.

Riding Statistics


In the statistics mode, users can view a detailed summary of their riding data. A graph on the right side displays the total odometer and trip distances for the week, offering a visual overview of their usage patterns. Below the graph, additional metrics like average speed, maximum speed, and average energy consumption (Wh/km) are shown, providing riders with a comprehensive understanding of their performance and efficiency.

Charging UI


The charging UI screen displays the estimated time remaining to fully charge the vehicle, along with the current charging percentage. This information helps users plan their charging sessions efficiently, ensuring they always know how long it will take to reach a full charge.

Visibility


To enhance usability, the dashboard offers both Light and Dark modes, allowing users to switch between them based on their preference and lighting conditions. Light Mode is ideal for daytime riding, providing clear visibility under bright sunlight, while Dark Mode reduces glare during nighttime or low-light situations, making it easier on the eyes. This flexibility ensures that users can always read the information on the dashboard comfortably, no matter the environment. By prioritizing visibility and adaptability, the design improves the overall riding experience, keeping users focused and informed.

Final Deliverable

With a fresh approach to the riding experience, users gained more control, comfort, and convenience. This design allowed them to seamlessly switch between modes, monitor key metrics, and personalize their settings, resulting in a smoother, more intuitive riding journey.

Challenges and Reflections

A key challenge in this project was managing user feedback; while riders wanted a wide range of information on the dashboard, displaying everything would have led to clutter and distraction. We had to prioritize which features were most essential, ensuring critical information remained accessible without overwhelming users. Integrating smooth transitions between ride modes and performance indicators also required precise design to maintain a cohesive experience.

Through this process, we learned the value of balancing user desires with practical design principles. By focusing on core needs and simplicity, we created a functional, user-friendly dashboard that enhances the riding experience. This project highlighted the importance of prioritization, user-centered design, and continuous iteration based on feedback.
